messages:
Alex: CrescentCare emailed back with their infosec questionnaire. They want the minimal network ask for the POC and asked whether PrivateLink or VPC peering is better. Also want sample firewall rules + rough connectivity cost differences.
Sofia: Quick Q: are they calling the hosted API (ours) or will this be a Private deployment inside their cloud?
Alex: Hosted API for the POC. They prefer a private path into our infra for compliance, so PrivateLink is the initial ask. Peering is under consideration if they move to a long-term Dedicated/private deployment.
Tom: Notes on tradeoffs: PrivateLink (interface endpoint) is fastest to provision and keeps traffic off the public internet. It terminates on our ENIs so the customer cannot see our backend IPs. PrivateLink does NOT preserve original client source IP when traffic enters our backend 12; connections are sourced from endpoint ENIs. VPC peering (or deploying Redwood in their account) preserves source IPs.
Priya: Infosec also asked: "Can you provide stable egress IPs for allowlisting?" For a PrivateLink POC we can provide the endpoint ENI EIPs (small stable set per region) post-provisioning. For public hosted API we recommend hostname allowlist or CDN prefix allowlist. For Dedicated/private we can guarantee fixed EIPs per contract.
Alex: They only allow IP allowlists (no DNS/SNI allowed). That increases setup time. Is PrivateLink still doable?
Tom: Yes, but we'll need to provision the interface endpoint and provide the ENI EIPs to them. Operational note: AWS may change the specific underlying EIPs on maintenance; we try to keep them stable but for strict IP-only policies we usually recommend a short contract with Dedicated or a peering arrangement if they need guaranteed static IPs. Flag this in sales.
Sofia: Firewall snippet for their netops (concise):
```
# Allow egress from app subnet to Redwood PrivateLink endpoint
- protocol: TCP
  port: 443
  destination: privatelink.us-east-1.api.redwood-inference.internal
  comment: TLS to Redwood PrivateLink endpoint. Replace with provided EIPs if IP-only policy.
- protocol: ICMP
  type: 3
  comment: Path MTU discovery (optional)
```
Alex: They asked for a one-line CMDB JSON entry to paste into their change ticket. Can we give that?
Tom: Sure, short example: 
```json
{"rule_name":"crescentcare->redwood-privatelink","direction":"egress","proto":"tcp","port":"443","dest":"<provided-eip-or-fqdn>","purpose":"POC to Redwood inference"}
```
Priya: Security answers to questionnaire bullets we'll include: TLS 1.2/1.3 in transit; we support HSTS; mutual TLS is only offered for Dedicated/private deployments as an enterprise feature; audit logs with request IDs available via Console; data plane traffic over PrivateLink is encrypted and isolated from public internet.
Sofia: Pricing bullet: PrivateLink costs = AWS interface endpoint hourly + AWS data processing per-GB + our connectivity maintenance surcharge (small). VPC peering = no endpoint hourly on AWS but potential cross-AZ data transfer and more setup overhead. For a short POC we usually recommend PrivateLink for speed.
Alex: They also want to know about SNI: their proxy performs SNI-based allowlisting. What hostname should they allow?
Tom: We'll give them SNI hostnames: e.g., privatelink.us-east-1.api.redwood-inference.internal (we also support wildcard certs). Tell them to allow TLS SNI for that host. If their proxy strips SNI, reach out and we can discuss alternative deployment.
Priya: Operational constraint to highlight to sales: if customer requires both "no DNS/SNI, only static IPs" and "preserve client source IP" that's not feasible without deploying Redwood in their account or setting up peering/transit into our VPC. Call that out as a blocker that needs an architecture decision.
Alex: Action items: (1) Confirm whether CrescentCare accepts the endpoint EIPs (we'll supply post-provision), (2) confirm SNI passthrough vs SNI block, (3) estimate POC bandwidth (GB/day) so Carol can estimate data-transfer costs.
Sofia: I'll work the questionnaire network items and draft the one-paragraph network section for their security team.
network-bot: Ticket NET-9123 created to provision sandbox PrivateLink in us-east-1 for CrescentCare POC. Owner: infra-oncall. ETA: 48 hours.
Alex: Perfect 12 I'll update CrescentCare, attach the firewall CMDB JSON, and ask for bandwidth numbers. If they push for src-IP preservation we'll escalate to propose peering or short-term Dedicated.
Tom: If they want strict IP stability > SLA, escalate to Sofia; we may need to offer a contract addendum.
Priya: I'll prepare the security snippets for the questionnaire (encryption, key mgmt assumptions, logging) and paste into the doc.
Alex: Thanks team 12 will loop back when CrescentCare replies.
